executive_briefing: Global tax policy in mid-2026 is defined by operational enforcement of the OECD Pillar Two 15% global minimum tax alongside aggressive trade tariff enforcement subject to key judicial challenges. ASEAN economies continue calibrating corporate tax incentives via non-taxable grants and territorial exemptions to preserve FDI competitiveness against global tax floors. Concurrently, indirect tax administrations are accelerating digital compliance through mandatory continuous transaction controls and phased Peppol e-invoicing networks.

trends.name: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Implementation
trends.summary: The OECD/G20 GloBE 15% global minimum tax framework is operational across major jurisdictions, enforcing a corporate tax floor on multinationals with annual revenues exceeding EUR 750 million to curb profit shifting.
evidence: The 15% GloBE corporate minimum tax is operational across Europe, APAC, and Inclusive Framework jurisdictions for multinational enterprises exceeding the 750 million EUR revenue threshold.
The OECD Corporate Income Tax Rates Database provides comprehensive 2026 rates and withholding tax benchmarks across all Inclusive Framework jurisdictions.
trends.reasoning: Sustained at Breakthrough as operational implementation of the 15% GloBE framework across Inclusive Framework countries solidifies baseline international corporate tax compliance.

trends.name: Unilateral Trade Tariffs and Judicial Challenges to Emergency Duty Regimes
trends.summary: Escalating trade tariffs and reciprocal duties face heightened legal scrutiny, exemplified by Court of International Trade rulings challenging emergency tariff declarations under executive authority.
evidence: The U.S. Court of International Trade ruled that certain trade tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) were unlawful, triggering appellate review.
Global trade management continues encountering friction from dynamic reciprocal duty schedules and shifting bilateral trade pact reviews.
trends.reasoning: Maintained in Peak Hype due to intense legal litigation, Supreme Court judicial anticipation, and operational supply chain restructuring across enterprise cross-border trade.

trends.name: ASEAN Territorial Tax Regimes and Strategic Incentives Calibration
trends.summary: ASEAN member states balance global minimum tax mandates by preserving competitive headline corporate tax rates alongside non-taxable CIT rebate grants and territorial exemptions to sustain enterprise investment.
evidence: Singapore maintains a 17% headline corporate tax rate while deploying structured CIT rebates and non-taxable grants to buffer qualified entities against top-up tax impacts.
The Grant Thornton ASEAN 6 Tax Guide 2026 outlines harmonized statutory updates and strategic corporate incentive recalibrations across key Southeast Asian markets.
trends.reasoning: Maintained in Breakthrough as regional tax authorities deploy targeted grant buffers and corporate income tax concessions to retain investment appeal amidst global minimum tax pressures.

trends.name: Mandatory Continuous Transaction Controls and Peppol E-Invoicing
trends.summary: Tax administrations globally accelerate mandatory continuous transaction controls and standardized Peppol e-invoicing networks to automate indirect tax auditing and prevent compliance leakage.
evidence: Singapore's IRAS and IMDA published updated statutory implementation timelines extending mandatory InvoiceNow GST e-invoicing requirements for businesses under the Peppol standard.
Revenue authorities internationally expand requirements for structured XML electronic invoices transmitted directly to tax portals for continuous transaction oversight.
trends.reasoning: Sustained at Breakthrough as mandatory statutory e-invoicing rollout schedules become established across revenue authorities globally.
